summary: Built and persisted an implementation-independent frontier-pressure oracle. Five static scenarios cover concurrent launch pressure, duplicate worker beacons, terminal/dedupe exclusion, live/stale-suspect heartbeat boundaries, and >=10m replaceable pressure. A standalone Node adapter self-checks fixture consistency and can compare a future compiler snapshot against the static expected outputs without importing production compiler logic.
tests: node frontier_pressure_oracle_v1.mjs frontier_pressure_oracle_v1.json -> ok=true, scenarios=5, mode=oracle-self-check
Fixture target values independently satisfy clamp(8, ceil(1.5 * distinct_recent_launches), 40).
Runner optionally accepts a candidate snapshot as a second argument and compares numeric outputs plus FRONTIER_THIN, RETURNS_UNCONSUMED and REPLACEABLE_PRESSURE trigger decisions.
Target paths were checked absent before append-only CREATE; no Current/Human Accepted/Served or production /w promotion was made.
unresolved: The live frontier-pressure compiler owner had not produced a terminal compiler snapshot during this run, so oracle-vs-actual comparison remains pending until that independent artifact exists.

acceptance: Run the compiler over equivalent oracle scenarios or adapt its snapshot to the documented scenario output shape.
All five scenarios match expected counts and trigger decisions.
